admission.justification: Weighed a shared warm index/explainer daemon against on-disk tree-keyed caches, constraining future serving architecture changes to measured latency triggers.

alternatives.option: Keep tree-keyed on-disk derived SQLite caches (open_cached_index) and per-process stdio explainer tool serving without a shared long-lived in-process index daemon.
alternatives.reason: Avoids a second long-lived stateful service and cross-seat cache invalidation bugs while keeping derived indexes disposable, read-only, and strictly keyed to exact Git memory trees (D1006, D1078).

alternatives.option: Host a shared warm in-process knowledge index and explainer serving daemon across concurrent MCP and explainer seats (D1006).
alternatives.reason: Adds daemon lifecycle, memory-retention, and cross-worktree isolation complexity without measured evidence that on-disk SQLite cache opens dominate seat latency.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Tool-call logs or startup benchmarks show repeated cold SQLite index opens or explainer cache rebuilds dominating Curator, Reviewer, or explainer turn latency across concurrent seats.

consequences: Derived knowledge indexes remain on-disk disposable caches keyed by memory tree hash.
Explainer seats remain isolated per-launch stdio servers bound to their launched seat marker.
context: Derived SQLite knowledge indexes are cached on disk by memory-tree key via memory/knowledge_index/cache.py and opened per process by MCP tools and explainer seats (canvas/explainer_server.py). Council #6 (D1078) and D1006 weighed keeping on-disk tree-keyed caches per stdio process versus hosting a shared warm in-process index and explainer service.
